_comment: cloud-ci-affected-set binding workspace-coverage policy (DATA, not code). ADR-0554, converts FRIC-1781310000: the only binding buck2 lane was scoped to //cloud/cloud-ci/..., so code anywhere else could merge broken (PR #651 head cf16525 did not compile yet its buck2 lane was green). ALL repo-specifics live here; the Rust kernel hardcodes no oyatie path and runs on any buck2 repo by editing this pack. full_trigger_patterns are the rdeps-cone ESCAPE classes — graph-semantic files whose blast radius the owner()/rdeps() derivation cannot model (build config, toolchains, vendored third-party, Starlark macros, the lockfile): any touch escalates to the FULL workspace, mechanically, with no skip and no human judgment. require_owner_patterns are the classes that MUST map to an owning target; an existing file in these classes with no owner FAILS the lane (graph-invisible code is not made safe by running more targets).
_full_trigger_note: Two seam classes here. (1) Build config/macros whose blast radius the per-package rdeps cone cannot bound — .buckconfig + .buckconfig.local + .buckconfig.d/** (all read by buck2, all committable), toolchains/**, third-party/** (reindeer vendor + fixups), Starlark **/*.bzl + **/*.bxl, rust-toolchain.toml. (2) Buildfiles and PACKAGE files are handled by package_definition_basenames (escalate to FULL on any change) AND mirrored here as **/PACKAGE so a NEW PACKAGE file (which evaluates to [] and would otherwise look like a plain no-owner file) is never a silent no-op. Cargo.lock is deliberately NOT a trigger: buck2 never reads it — a dependency change that affects buck2 semantics MUST touch third-party/**; the cargo lanes + ADR-0539 freshness gate own lock hygiene.
_package_sibling_note: Cargo.toml + build.rs are NOT buck2 graph inputs (buck2 never reads them; reindeer/BUCK mirror them) and have no owner() BY DESIGN, so requiring an owner would refuse every manifest edit (proven by this lane's own first dogfood run). They are semantically bound to their crate, so they seed the ENCLOSING package target pattern; if that package does not exist the seed query fails and the lane escalates to FULL.
_package_definition_note: Ground-truth buck2 buildfile-name set in PRECEDENCE order: BUCK.v2 SHADOWS BUCK when both exist (empirically verified against this buck2 binary — adding an empty BUCK.v2 next to a real BUCK drops the BUCK targets). A change to ANY buildfile escalates to FULL (these basenames are also escape-class): a buildfile edit can add/remove targets or shadow the file dependents load, so its blast radius is NOT bounded by its own package's rdeps. owner() is empty for a buildfile by design, so seeding 'its package' alone would silently miss every dependent (F2). If buck2's [buildfile] name/extra_for_test config ever adds names, mirror them here — this list IS the repo's buildfile-name ground truth, not a single hand-set name.
_synthetic_dependencies_note: ADR-0554 round-6 (defect 2): every changed path must map to a buck2 owner() OR an explicit synthetic-dependency declaration here, otherwise it escalates to FULL (an unowned, undeclared path is derivation uncertainty — the old silent 'docs class — fine' default was a selector hole). Each key is a micro-glob; the value is the list of synthetic seed targets the path contributes (a whole-tree-scanner input declared as a graph edge). An EMPTY list is an explicit inert declaration: 'this class is not a buck2 graph input.' A declaration only applies when owner() is EMPTY — an owned instance (e.g. an include_str! markdown asset) is still seeded by owner(), so declaring docs inert never shadows a real owner. CONSERVATIVE by design: only clearly-inert, commonly-touched doc classes are declared, so a docs-only PR stays fast; EVERYTHING ELSE unowned (yaml/toml/json/txt config, unknown extensions) escalates to FULL until a class earns an evidence-backed declaration. Broadening this map is an optimization follow-up, never a soundness requirement.
_github_seed_note: `.github/**` is the canonical whole-tree-scanner input: owner() is empty for it BY DEFINITION (it is nobody's declared src), which is the PREMISE of a synthetic declaration, not evidence of inertness. Two cheaper shapes were tried and reverted. (1) Declaring it INERT (`[]`) is a FALSE GREEN — a dozen gate tests read `.github/**` at runtime by climbing from cwd to a repo-root marker, and a workflow-only PR resolved to NoGraphTargets and walked past the no-new-shell ratchet (PR #1389, reverted by #1391). (2) Making it OWNED (export_file + $(location)) is subtler but also wrong: resolve() SHORT-CIRCUITS on a non-empty owner() (`seeds.extend(owners); continue`) and never reaches synthetic_seeds(), so owning these paths permanently DISABLES this mechanism for them and narrows the cone to the export's own rdeps. The seeds below are PACKAGE patterns, not individual targets: a package pattern is robust to target renames and is a strict SUPERSET of the specific test targets that read the tree — over-seeding costs build time, under-seeding is a merge-authority hole. The list is not hand-trusted: ci-affected-target-set-github-consumer-coverage derives the consumer set FROM THE TREE (a quote-anchored `.github` path literal in a .rs/.json under a rust_test-bearing buck2 package) and fails closed on any package missing here, so consumer N+1 cannot land unwired. `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes` and `**/OWNERS` are deliberately NOT declared — no consumer was verified for them, so they keep escalating to FULL (the safe default). ONE seed is deliberately un-derivable and must not be deleted just because the completeness gate stays green without it: root//ci/facade/artifact-inventory-registry: (the accounting producer) names no `.github` literal at all — it consumes `git ls-files` verbatim, so every tracked `.github` path becomes an accounting row and an add/remove/edit there can flip ci-baseline-ratchet-gate through the frozen baseline + signoff. Its cone was measured to be a strict subset of the derived seeds' cone (zero added targets), so pinning it makes that coverage explicit at zero build cost instead of accidental. UN-DERIVABLE CLASS, enumerated deliberately: five packages consume `git ls-files` verbatim rather than naming a `.github` literal, so the completeness gate can never derive them. `artifact-inventory-registry`, `scm-facts-snapshot` (src/lib.rs:3527, tracked-paths universe moved verbatim from the producer's old git_ls_files), `artifact-accountability`, `crate-registration`, and `inventory-registry-drift` all flow a tracked `.github` add/remove/edit into accounting rows and can flip `ci-baseline-ratchet-gate`. Four of them are in the cone TODAY only transitively, via a dependency edge on a declared seed — exactly the accidental coverage this note rejects, and ADR-0552's scm-facts/accounting split is actively refactoring that edge. Measured cost of pinning all five: ZERO added targets (each already in the cone). Pinning converts accidental coverage into stated coverage at no build cost.
_inert_selection_classes_note: PREDICATE (1) of the selection-totality assertion: a NON-EMPTY diff that selects NO targets is a target-determination bug, never a pass — the lane would report success having built and tested NOTHING, i.e. green precisely BECAUSE it checked nothing. This list is the ONLY licence for that outcome: a diff consisting solely of these classes may legitimately select nothing (a docs-only PR). It is deliberately NOT derived from the `[]` entries in synthetic_dependencies, because those two statements differ — `synthetic_dependencies[X] = []` says 'X contributes no seed', this list says 'X may be the ENTIRE selection and still pass'. PR #1389 is the proof the split matters: `.github/**: []` was defensible as the first statement and a merge-authority hole as the second (a workflow-only PR resolved to NoGraphTargets and walked past the no-new-shell ratchet). With the split, adding a broad class to synthetic_dependencies as `[]` now FAILS RED naming the path instead of passing green; granting it an empty selection takes a second, single-purpose, reviewed line here. GROWING THIS LIST IS A MERGE-AUTHORITY CHANGE — an entry asserts the class can affect NO buck2 target whatsoever, and being wrong is silent. Absent field = empty = fail-closed (any non-empty diff that selects nothing is refused).

product_contract.born_pack_shaped: The escape-trigger classes, owner-required classes, universe, full-run patterns, cell roots, and base ref are DATA here; the Rust kernel hardcodes no repo path nor any oyatie string (R0, ADR-0548). The kernel DOES fix the decision SEMANTICS — RefuseUnowned > Full > Affected > NoGraphTargets dominance, derivation-uncertainty-escalates-to-full, owner() on every existing changed file regardless of extension — that contract is the engine, not a per-repo pack value.
product_contract.fail_closed: Derivation NEVER skips: git/uquery/rdeps errors, unmappable package files, deleted graph files, and empty rdeps closures all escalate to the full workspace run. The only hard failures are an unreadable/invalid pack, owner-required files with no owning target, and the build/test verdict itself.
product_contract.tiers: pull_request -> auto (affected cone, escalation binding); merge_group + push + workflow_dispatch -> full (admission/integration tier per ADR-0515 Tide direction).
product_contract.precedent: Bazel target determination / bazel-diff (Tinder), Meta/Google affected-target CI; reimplemented Rust-native on buck2 uquery owner()/rdeps() per the proven-patterns doctrine.
product_contract.execution: Buck2-native Rust lane; no shell logic beyond the workflow YAML step (G011 Rust-successor that RETIRED the transitional infra/ci/buck2-affected-gate.sh shell driver, removed ADR-0554 round-6).

purpose: Binding workspace coverage: every PR builds+tests the buck2 reverse-dependency cone of its merge-base diff as a REQUIRED context, with mechanical fail-closed escalation to the full workspace whenever the cone cannot be trusted. Any owner-required source change with a buck2 target builds+tests its cone; any buildfile/config/macro change escalates to FULL; a genuinely-unowned owner-required file (e.g. a source in a sub-workspace buck2 does not model) REFUSES the merge until it is wired — never silently passes.
